scope.question: Can a new private proof, limited to one original resume_intent call and current generation, safely reuse a completed account graph across precisely controlled non-account cursor transactions without changing existing receipts, storage authority, crash/cut/cancellation semantics or live checks?
scope.named_tests_below: Retained source-level contracts, not newly executed controls.
scope.not_a_universal_impossibility_claim: A different enforced writer ownership and dependency observation design could be separately proposed and qualified. Current trace/owner alone does not provide that design.

decision.decisive_gap: The proposed certificate must cross COMMIT gaps where the original SQLite writer lock is released. A raw second SQLite connection is within the retained fault surface. The current connection-local trace cannot observe its attempted no-row writes or rolled-back writes. Unchanged current graph bytes, state, generation and data_version do not certify the absence of those required invalidation events. This is a static coverage/indistinguishability argument; no new exploit or native negative control was run.
decision.data_version_limit: The pinned SQLite source uses u32 pager/Btree data-version arithmetic, not a globally monotone checked event journal. Reading that value into u64 does not create sticky overflow detection or history of foreign attempted SQL. Equality is a useful change observation but insufficient for all requested invalidation facts.
decision.existing_receipt_not_relaxed: PostWriteReadback remains restricted to its actual original writer and no-write epoch. It must not be re-stamped after COMMIT or after a permitted-looking statement, and a partial frontier must not become a whole-graph receipt.
decision.cost_benefit: There is real repeated account-graph work in the retained workload, but its 71 account_graph calls combine full/partial roles and imports. No per-role saved-cost estimate or cross-cursor candidate performance was measured. The observed cost does not justify weakening the above invalidation contract.

findings.finding: Node owner.lock is cooperative process ownership, not continuous exclusion of arbitrary SQLite writers. Every original atomic_reorg_with_readback commits before the next cursor cut/transaction. The retained foreign-writer test explicitly opens a raw second connection, proves DatabaseBusy under the original writer, then mutates archive_nodes after commit and requires owner stop on the fresh read.

evidence.fact: owner.lock ownership and WAL database setup
BEGIN IMMEDIATE, original owner and final write fences, COMMIT
original_write_lock_blocks_foreign_writer_and_no_scope_survives_commit
Another connection has a separate observer and does not change this observer

findings.consequence: The new proof cannot safely treat a same-generation owner.lock holder as a certificate that no foreign operation happened between cursor transactions. Retaining an SQLite writer lock across the gaps would change the original transaction/cut contract rather than solve this inside the proposed private proof.

findings.finding: The actual bundled SQLite 3.51.3 source stores Pager.iDataVersion as u32, increments it without checked sticky overflow, returns it as u32, and combines it with per-Btree iBDataVersion. Own commits compensate the local Btree offset. It is computed by the pager, not a durable global database revision.

pinned_source_lines.82847-82864: Not stored in database; u32 result is pager version plus Btree offset

not_claimed: No wrap was observed or executed.
No claim that one increment equals one foreign transaction.
No external no-row or rollback experiment was run.
findings.required_but_not_sufficient_sampling: If used as one defense in a future design, sample on the same connection after acquiring the next actual BEGIN IMMEDIATE and before reuse; do not sample only before acquiring the lock, and do not reset the certificate after an observed mismatch. This still does not prove all required events absent.

findings.finding: Current STMT observation provides private connection/process identity and checked statement/write/control counters. It intentionally counts attempted writes before their outcome. It does not expose table dependencies, bound parameters, affected rows, successful completion, or a token binding one statement to an authorized owner operation. A counter delta cannot distinguish an approved cursor mutation from an unknown write with the same count.

evidence.fact: Private owner state, single trace installation, live probe, attempted execution counters
Same actual WRITE transaction and no potentially writing SQL since capture
Failed/no-row/reversed DDL and prepared writes remain invalidating

findings.precompiled_statement_assessment: Already prepared/reused statements are observed at execution by the existing trace. This is a supported capability, not a missed-existing-statement bug. A new preparation-only SQL authorizer would not by itself replace the original execution evidence.

precompiled_evidence.fact: Cached/prepared controls and writes observed at execution

findings.new_design_obligations: Any new local dependency journal would need exact privately nominated statement identity and operation lifetime, bounded bindings and expected affected-row checks, successful completion acknowledgment, sticky rejection of all other writes/controls, and independent observer liveness. That is a new ownership protocol; none is supplied by the existing write counter.

findings.finding: SQLite allows one trace callback per connection; a second trace replaces the first. The current native boundary installs an authorizer and the cancellation cleanup installs another specialized authorizer/progress handler. New hook installation must be integrated under the existing owner and lifecycle. It cannot assume hooks compose or overwrite an existing policy.

pinned_source_lines.3885-3903: STMT is beginning-of-statement; PROFILE supplies completion timing, not a full successful-row proof
pinned_source_lines.3934-3937: Trace registrations override previous trace callbacks
pinned_source_lines.11008-11024: Preupdate hook requires compile feature and has table coverage restrictions
pinned_source_lines.124180-124193: set_authorizer replaces callback/context and may expire prepared statements

Specialized cleanup authorizer/progress ownership and cleanup
Replacing trace is detected by a real execution probe

findings.consequence: Per-row hooks also miss no-row/failed statements and do not observe other connections. They cannot replace the current attempted-execution fencing. This review does not assert the preupdate feature is already enabled or qualified.

findings.finding: The existing contract explicitly excludes general immutability for prepare-time PRAGMA effects, Blob/backup, indirect UDF/virtual-table effects. PostWriteReadback freshly checks ordinary main/temp schema and executes writable_schema=RESET through DONE before its first graph, handling catalog/cached-VM divergence. Equal final catalog or schema_version cannot alone prove no unknown/DDL/ABA action happened across a released transaction.

evidence.fact: Declared coverage boundary
Fresh namespace/schema and RESET normalization
Retained catalog and cached-VM divergence negative control source

findings.consequence: A future proof must retain actual schema/VM normalization, no extra attached or temp objects, original ordinary tables, and fail closed on unsupported API/SQL. This does not repair the foreign-history gap.

findings.finding: The durable intent transaction and its cut finish before the original resume_intent_with_progress call. A proof confined to that call cannot inherit the intent graph. During the cursor loop active remains (old,g-1), while the final transaction publishes active generation g. A current-generation proof cannot be silently rebound to g across that publication.

evidence.fact: Intent commit and cut precede resume call
Fresh durable row, active generation check and steps check
Separate immediate transaction and commit-before-cut per cursor
Fresh final state checks and atomic active/generation/slot publication

findings.consequence: Do not describe all nine original transactions as reusable under a one-resume/current-generation scope. Any hypothetical eligible prepublication cursor subsequence would require its own independently established proof, and final publication invalidates it.

findings.finding: Current State/Record/delta/full commitment comparison, original row preimages and rowcount guards, actual transaction completion, final owner and write fences, cancellation/Host checks, crash cuts and durable cursor remain mandatory. Whole-graph mathematical equality is not an authority to accept stale storage or replace current input checks.

evidence.fact: Bounded role nomination; fresh complete-state check; whole graph only; consumed-result and last-write fences
Partial frontier does not nominate a whole graph
Delta preimage, rowcount and progress checks
Typed cancellation selection and cleanup against actual durable cursor
Original acceptance/source/workload/budget and semantic boundaries

findings.relation_to_group_commit: The separate group-commit review rejects changed durable prefixes/cuts/cancelled_cursor. A dependency proof that preserved those boundaries is a distinct proposal, but it still fails the observation/ownership sufficiency conditions above. This review does not propose grouping commits.

measurement_limits.retained_workload_context: The independently retained H4-to-H11 case has intent + seven attach transactions + final publication. Account-root repetition is an opportunity signal; State and non-account roots still vary.
measurement_limits.graph_aggregate: 71 account_graph calls and their nested time combine different full/partial roles across imports. This review does not assign all calls or all time to cursor transactions or forecast savings.
measurement_limits.host_aggregate: 29,928 Host checkpoints belong to the whole complete-page import, not activation alone; thread CPU is nested and cannot be added to caller CPU or used as an exact percentage.

possible_future_direction_without_approv.boundary: Only a separately specified and measured ownership/dependency design that actually supplies the missing external event or exclusion proof could reopen cross-cursor reuse. It must retain all current foreign-writer, rollback, no-row, schema, generation, source, cancellation and durable-prefix behavior.
not_sufficient: Same accountRoot or unchanged active generation alone
Allowed table names or the number of executed writes alone
Re-stamping PostWriteReadback after an allowed-looking operation
A new trace/authorizer installed beside existing hooks
Promoting partial graph receipts or cached authorization
possible_future_direction_without_approv.smaller_existing_boundary: If exploring independent improvements, keep them inside a currently proven writer/no-write epoch or a single immutable input computation, preserve actual current observations, and measure their own cost before production changes. No implementation recommendation or performance qualification is made here.
